(4-alpha-a)/(3-alpha)=(3-a)/2. No H(2H-1) factor enters, and sqrt(c) is the unit-noise coefficient. c is kept distinct from OC's auxiliary label in S_c.

checks.claim: Physical pairing: bridge definition (1) gives B(f^2,f^2)=c int f^4 on full H1, so R_sp and E_sp in note (1) are the parent objects at alpha=1.
checks.reason: With nu=dx c delta_0(dy), B(f,h)=c int f h. R(g)=A_sp/b^(alpha/2) becomes c int f^4/||f'||_2 and E_sp=sup(A_sp-b/2), matching bridge Section 4 and OC Section 6. No Fourier factor or |x|^-1 density enters.

checks.claim: Locally AC representative, q=f^2 and q'=2ff' in L1.
checks.reason: The primitive of f' in L1_loc differs from f by a function with zero weak derivative. Every zero-integral test function is the derivative of a compact smooth primitive, so that function is a.e. constant, and continuous representatives patch uniquely. The product of locally AC functions is locally AC. q'=2ff' a.e., and Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||q'||_1<=2||f||_2||f'||_2. Only textbook sub-steps are left implicit (see minor findings).

checks.claim: Global limits 0, boundedness, f^4 integrability, and F being C^1 with F'=q, endpoints 0 and 1, and 0<=F<=1.
checks.reason: Tail integrability of q' gives Cauchy limits at both infinities, and q>=0 in L1 forces both to be 0. A continuous q with zero limits is bounded, so A<=||q||_inf. q is continuous, so the fundamental theorem gives F in C^1. Unit mass and monotone limits give the endpoints. No positivity of f, strict increase of F or compact support is used.

checks.claim: Mixed integral int f'f(1-2F)=A, sign and coefficient included, with finite-R limits.
checks.reason: (q(1-2F))'=q'(1-2F)-2q^2 is in L1. Boundary terms vanish because q->0 and |1-2F|<=1. Letting R->infinity gives int q'(1-2F)=2A, hence 2 int ff'(1-2F)=2A with a positive sign.

checks.claim: CDF term int f^2(1-2F)^2=1/3.
checks.reason: P(y)=y-2y^2+(4/3)y^3 has P'=(1-2y)^2. P(F) is C^1 with derivative q(1-2F)^2<=q, integrable. P(1)-P(0)=1-2+4/3=1/3. Flat intervals of F cause no difficulty.

checks.claim: Square expansion for EVERY real z: int[f'-z f(1-2F)]^2=b-2zA+z^2/3>=0.
checks.reason: Both summands are in L2 because |1-2F|<=1. The cross term is absolutely integrable by Cauchy-Schwarz, so the pointwise a.e. expansion integrates term by term with no infinite subtraction. Coefficients are -2z times A and z^2 times 1/3.

checks.claim: cdf_square_bound application: (6) supplies the exact Lean premise after analytic derivation, with A=int f^4 and b=int(f')^2.
checks.reason: The printed pp.all type is (b-((2*z)*A))+(z^2/3)>=0 for all real z, identical to (6)'s right side, with Real variables and Nat exponents. Hand check of the application only: z=3A gives b-3A^2>=0. The kernel proves only this finite step, and the note says so.

checks.reason: f^4=0 a.e. would force f=0 a.e., contradicting unit norm. The note asserts A>0 without that sentence (minor finding). b=0 forces a constant representative, and the only L2 constant is 0. 3A^2<=b with b>0 gives the ratio bound.

checks.claim: Sech profile integrals: f_ell is real smooth H1, with mass 1, int f^4=ell/3 and int(f')^2=ell^2/3.
checks.reason: f'=-ell tanh(ell x) f. With t=tanh(ell x) and dt=ell sech^2(ell x)dx: (ell/2)sech^2 dx=(1/2)dt, f^4 dx=(ell/4)(1-t^2)dt, (f')^2 dx=(ell^2/2)t^2 dt. Integrating on (-1,1) gives 1, ell/3 and ell^2/3. Independent cross-check: 1-2F=-tanh(ell x), so the square in (6) vanishes pointwise at z=ell=3A.

checks.claim: E_sp=c^2/6 for c>0, using energy_upper and sech attainment at ell=c.

At ell=c, cA-b/2=c^2/3-c^2/6=c^2/6, by an admissible full-H1 profile. Cross-check: bridge (17) at alpha=1 gives E_sp=R_sp^2/2=c^2/6.

OC (2) and bridge (18) at q=3, k=2, 2-alpha=1 give this map. (2E_sp)^(1/2)=c/sqrt3. The bracket is c/(sqrt3*8*3^(3/2))=c/72. Then 2 sqrt(c/72)=sqrt(c)/(3sqrt2), and 2^(3/2) times this equals (2/3)sqrt(c).
